question: Should ClawHub prohibit crypto, blockchain, finance, and trading listings categorically, or regulate them by observable behavior and risk?
rationale: Current main implements contextual spam, malicious-content, and financial-abuse rules but does not choose the RFC's category-wide marketplace boundary; that choice requires product and security intent.

options.title: Behavior-Based Boundary
options.body: Disallow deceptive, unsafe, or unapproved financial actions while permitting clearly described lower-risk identity, registry, reputation, educational, and read-only uses.

options.title: Category-Wide Prohibition
options.body: Exclude crypto, blockchain, finance, and trading listings from the public registry regardless of narrower behavior or safeguards.

options.title: Default-Deny Exceptions
options.body: Hold these categories for human review and enumerate narrow permitted cases in public policy.

recommendation.title: Behavior-Based Boundary
recommendation.body: Disallow deceptive, unsafe, or unapproved financial actions while permitting clearly described lower-risk identity, registry, reputation, educational, and read-only uses.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen authored this RFC and the recent public acceptable-usage clarification, giving him the strongest direct policy history.
